meanings: pay no attention to the barking
forms: literally: the dog barks, the wind carries it off

examples.sr: Не секирај се због критика: [па̑с ла̏је̄, ве̏тар но̀си].
examples.en: Don't worry about the criticism: the dog barks, the wind carries it off.

note: The wind carries the barking away: criticism is not worth minding.

examples.sr: Он [ла̏же ка̏о па̑с], не верујем му.
examples.en: He lies through his teeth, I don't believe him.

meanings: to be left without a roof over one's head

examples.sr: После пожара многе породице су [о̀стале без кро̏ва над гла́во̄м].
examples.en: After the fire, many families were left without a roof over their heads.

examples.sr: Никоме не причај, [не̏ка то̑ о̀стане̄ ме̏ђу на̏ма].
examples.en: Don't tell anyone, let this stay between us.

examples.sr: Помогао ми је, а ја [не́ћу о̀стати ду́жан].
examples.en: He helped me, and I won't stay in his debt.

note: Can mean repaying a favor or taking revenge, depending on context.

examples.sr: Младић је био толико затечен да је [о̀стао без ре̑чи].
examples.en: The young man was so taken aback that he was left speechless.

meanings: nothing else was left for me

examples.sr: [Нѝје нам о̀стало ни̏шта дру̏го] него да чекамо.
examples.en: We have no choice but to wait.

examples.sr: Мислим да смо [и̏зравнали ра̀чуне].
examples.en: I think we're even.

note: Used both literally (to pay back a debt) and figuratively (to end a dispute, to get even).

forms: literally: a bill without the innkeeper

examples.sr: Све сте испланирали, али [пра̀вите ра̀чӯн без кр̏чмара].
examples.en: You've planned everything, but it looks like you're counting your chickens before they hatch.

note: You cannot settle up at an inn without asking the innkeeper: counting on something without the key person. Close to «counting your chickens».

examples.sr: Сви морају да [по̀ложе ра̀чӯн] за своје поступке.
examples.en: Everyone must answer for their actions.

note: Impf. «полагати рачуне»: «теби не морам полагати рачуне» - I don't have to answer to you.

forms: literally: to hang by a hair

examples.sr: Његов живот је [ви̏сио о дла̏ци].
examples.en: His life was hanging by a thread.

forms: literally: to go against the fur

examples.sr: Не треба му [ѝћи уз дла̏ку] кад је љут.
examples.en: You shouldn't cross him when he's angry.

note: The paired expression «ићи низ длаку» means to agree with someone, to flatter.

meanings: to get someone back on their feet

examples.sr: Лекари су га после дуге болести [по̀дигли на но̏ге].
examples.en: The doctors got him back on his feet after a long illness.

examples.sr: Концерт је [по̀дигао на но̏ге] цео град.
examples.en: The concert got the whole city on its feet.

examples.sr: Цео дан сам [на но̀гама].
examples.en: I've been on my feet all day.

examples.sr: Попио је кафу [с но̏гу] и отишао на посао.
examples.en: He drank his coffee on the go and left for work.

note: Said of quick eating and drinking when there is no time to sit down.

forms: literally: from small feet

examples.sr: Бавим се музиком [од ма̀лих но̏гу].
examples.en: I've been doing music since I was little.

examples.sr: Са свим колегама живи [на до̀број но̀зи].
examples.en: He's on good terms with all his colleagues.

meanings: to live high on the hog
forms: literally: to live on a high foot

examples.sr: Почео је да [жи̏ви на висо̀кој но̀зи].
examples.en: He started to live in grand style.

examples.sr: Грип ју је потпуно [обо̀рио с но̏гу].
examples.en: The flu completely knocked her off her feet.

examples.sr: Вест о победи га је [о̀борила с но̏гу].
examples.en: The news of the victory floored him.

meanings: a lie is soon found out

examples.sr: Не лажи, јер [у ла̏жи су кра̀тке но̏ге].
examples.en: Don't lie, because lies have short legs.

note: A deception is soon uncovered and does not get you far.

forms: literally: to hide like a snake hides its legs

examples.sr: Он [кри̏је сво̀је на̑мере ка̏о змѝја но̏ге].
examples.en: He is hiding his intentions very carefully.

note: If a snake had legs, it would hide them very skillfully.

examples.sr: Ако желиш да живиш овде, поштоваћеш [ку̏ћнӣ ре̑д].
examples.en: If you want to live here, you'll follow the house rules.

examples.sr: Она је [у пр̏вим рѐдовима] међу младим научницима.
examples.en: She is in the front ranks of the young scientists.

examples.sr: И ти ћеш [до́ћи на ре̑д], само полако.
examples.en: Your turn will come too, take it easy.

examples.sr: Афера је [ба̏цила се̏нку на] његову каријеру.
examples.en: The scandal cast a shadow on his career.

examples.sr: Новинари су глумицу [пра̏тили ка̏о се̑нка].
examples.en: Reporters followed the actress like a shadow.

meanings: to be afraid of one's own shadow

examples.sr: Не сме ништа да уради, [пла̏ши се сво̀је се̑нке].
examples.en: He doesn't dare to do anything, he's afraid of his own shadow.

note: Variant: «бојати се властите сенке».

meanings: a shadow of one's former self

examples.sr: После болести је био само [се̑нка од чо̀века].
examples.en: After the illness he was only a shadow of a man.

examples.sr: Он је [из се̑нке] утицао на све одлуке.
examples.en: He influenced all the decisions from the shadows.

examples.sr: Кад останем сам ноћу, [хва̏та ме стра̑х].
examples.en: When I'm alone at night, I get scared.

note: Pattern «хвата ме + feeling»: носталгија, језа, грозница (nostalgia, a shiver, a fever).

examples.sr: Причао је виц и сви су [хва̏тали за сто̏ма̄к].
examples.en: He was telling a joke and everyone was holding their sides.

note: Usually «хватати се за стомак од смеха».

examples.sr: Изгледа да [се хва̏таш за сла̏мку].
examples.en: It looks like you're clutching at straws.

examples.sr: Секретарица је [хва̏тала бѐлешке] током састанка.
examples.en: The secretary took notes during the meeting.

examples.sr: Не [хва̏тај крѝвине], има посла за све.
examples.en: Don't shirk, there's work for everyone.

note: Colloquial: to pretend to be busy and avoid work.

forms: literally: to catch the fog

examples.sr: Чим је видео полицију, [у̀хватио је ма̏глу].
examples.en: As soon as he saw the police, he ran off.

note: Colloquial. More often pf.: ухватити маглу.

meanings: to pay out of one's own pocket

examples.sr: Мораћу [да пла̀тим из сво̑г џе̏па].
examples.en: I'll have to pay out of my own pocket.

meanings: to hit someone in the wallet

examples.sr: Нова такса ће нас [у̀дарити по џѐпу].
examples.en: The new fee will hit us in the wallet.

examples.sr: Они су покушали да [и̏спразне џѐпове] верника.
examples.en: They tried to empty the believers' pockets.

examples.sr: Дошао је у град [пра̏зних џѐпова].
examples.en: He came to the city penniless.

forms: literally: deep pockets

examples.sr: Она тражи неког са [ду̀боким џѐповима].
examples.en: She is looking for someone with deep pockets.

examples.sr: То није [за сва̏чијӣ џе̏п].
examples.en: That isn't within everyone's means.

meanings: to know like the back of one's hand
forms: literally: to know like one's own pocket

examples.sr: Познајем ово место [ка̏о сво̑ј џе̏п].
examples.en: I know this place like the back of my hand.

meanings: I have a problem (opening a request to a repairman)

examples.sr: [Ѝма̄м јѐдан про̀бле̄м]. Можете ли да ми помогнете?
examples.en: I have a problem. Can you help me?

note: A calm opening with a repairman or support; then you briefly say what happened.

examples.sr: [Цу̏ри сла̀вина] у купатилу.
examples.en: The faucet in the bathroom is leaking.

note: Similar complaints: «пукла је цев» - a pipe burst; «не ради бојлер» - the water heater is out.

meanings: I would like you to ... for me (request to a repairman)

examples.sr: [Жѐлео бих да ми за̀мените] бојлер.
examples.en: I'd like you to replace the water heater.

examples.sr: [Жѐлела бих да ми о̀кречите] зид.
examples.en: I'd like you to paint the wall.

note: Polite request: after «да ми» the verb takes the plural «you» form («замените») as a sign of politeness.

meanings: I'd like to book an appointment with ...

examples.sr: [Жѐлим да за̀кажем пре́глед ко̏д] гинеколога.
examples.en: I'd like to book an appointment with a gynecologist.

examples.sr: [Зака̀зала бих пре́глед ко̏д] докторке Савић.
examples.en: I'd like to book an appointment with Dr. Savić.

note: On the phone, first check the office («Да ли је то стоматолошка ординација?»). «код» + gen.

examples.sr: [Одго̀вара ми] сутра у 12.
examples.en: Tomorrow at 12 works for me.

examples.sr: [Не одго̀вара ми] овај термин.
examples.en: This time slot doesn't work for me.

key: phr:да ли постоји могућност кућне посете
meanings: is it possible to arrange a home visit?

examples.sr: [Да ли по̀стоји могу́ћно̄ст ку̏ћне по̀сете?]
examples.en: Is it possible for the doctor to make a home visit?

note: A home-call service is «теренска служба»; an exam at home is «преглед на терену».

forms: literally: to circle like a cat around bacon

examples.sr: Већ сат времена [кру̀жи ка̏о ма̏чка о̏ко сла̀нине], а не усуђује се да пита.
examples.en: He's been beating around the bush for an hour and doesn't dare to ask.

forms: literally: the old woman with the cakes has passed by

examples.sr: Сада је касно, [про̏шла ба̏ба с кола̀чима].
examples.en: It's too late now, the ship has sailed.

forms: literally: bread with seven crusts

examples.sr: За њих је сваки динар [хле̏б са се̏дам ко̑ра].
examples.en: For them every dinar is hard-earned bread.

note: Said of income that took a lot of hard work to earn.

meanings: to mess things up for someone
forms: literally: to brown the soup

examples.sr: Неко нам је [за̀пржио чо́рбу].
examples.en: Someone has messed things up for us.

examples.sr: Сам си себи [за̀пржио чо́рбу].
examples.en: You've messed things up for yourself.

note: The image of a ruined soup: the roux is burnt and cannot be fixed.

examples.sr: Његова мајка је била [ѝзван се̏бе] од бриге.
examples.en: His mother was beside herself with worry.

examples.sr: Дајем ти пар дана да [до̀ђеш к се̏би].
examples.en: I'm giving you a few days to pull yourself together.

examples.sr: Он је [прѐузео на се̏бе] сву одговорност.
examples.en: He took all the responsibility upon himself.

examples.sr: Седела је у тишини, [у̀дубљена у се̏бе].
examples.en: She sat in silence, lost in thought.

examples.sr: Током разговора [по̀вукао се у се̏бе] и ћутао.
examples.en: During the conversation he retreated into his shell and said nothing.

examples.sr: Овај проблем [сам по се̏би] није тежак.
examples.en: This problem in itself is not hard.

note: «сам» declines: сама по себи, само по себи.

examples.sr: [Ца̑рство му не̏беско], био је добар човек.
examples.en: God rest his soul, he was a good man.

note: A religious condolence formula, fitting when the other person is religious.

examples.sr: [Бо̑г да по̀мене] нашег деду.
examples.en: God rest our grandfather's soul.

note: A religious formula said in memory of the dead. Not for non-religious listeners.

examples.sr: [По̀чивао у ми̏ру], драги пријатељу.
examples.en: Rest in peace, dear friend.

note: For a woman: «почивала у миру».

forms: literally: water comes to my mouth

examples.sr: Кад осетим мирис ћевапа, [и̏де ми во̀да на у́ста].
examples.en: When I smell ćevapi, my mouth waters.

meanings: to take the bread out of someone's mouth

examples.sr: Тим порезима су људима [о̀тели за̏лога̄ј из у́ста].
examples.en: Those taxes took the bread out of people's mouths.

meanings: to put words in someone's mouth

examples.sr: Немој да ми [ста̀вљаш ре̑чи у у́ста].
examples.en: Don't put words in my mouth.

key: phr:из уста си ми извадио реч
meanings: you took the words right out of my mouth

examples.sr: [Из у́ста си ми ѝзвадио ре̑ч]!
examples.en: You took the words right out of my mouth!

examples.sr: Ставио је [пр̏ст на у́ста] да ућутимо.
examples.en: He put a finger to his lips to make us be quiet.

key: phr:из твојих уста у божје уши
meanings: from your mouth to God's ears

examples.sr: Победићемо? - [Из тво̀јӣх у́ста у бо̏жје у̏ши]!
examples.en: Are we going to win? - From your mouth to God's ears!

note: A reply to a good hope or wish: may God hear you.

examples.sr: О томе се причало [на сва̏ у́ста].
examples.en: It was talked about openly.

examples.sr: Он те хвали [на сва̏ у́ста].
examples.en: He sings your praises to everyone.

meanings: to be always on someone's lips

examples.sr: Та реченица им [не сѝлази с у́ста].
examples.en: That phrase never leaves their lips.

examples.sr: Немој да [прѝказујеш све̏ цр̀ним бо̀јама], није све тако лоше.
examples.en: Don't paint everything in dark colors, it's not that bad.

meanings: to see everything through dark glasses

examples.sr: Људи у депресији [гле̏дајӯ све̑т кроз цр̀не на̏оча̄ре].
examples.en: Depressed people see the world through dark glasses.

examples.sr: Његово име је на [цр̀ној ли̑сти].
examples.en: His name is on the blacklist.

examples.sr: Радим већ двадесет година и [је̏де̄м сво̑ј хле̏б].
examples.en: I've been working for twenty years and I earn my own living.

note: Echoes the Bible: «in the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread».

examples.sr: Не желим да [је̏де̄м ту̏ђ хле̏б].
examples.en: I don't want to live off other people.

note: Sometimes with a hint of betrayal: he ate their bread, then turned against them.

meanings: to laze around waiting for everything to be handed over
forms: literally: lie down, bread, so I can eat you

examples.sr: Он само [ле̏зи ле̏бе да те је̏де̄м] и чека да му неко све донесе.
examples.en: He just lazes around and waits for someone to bring him everything.

note: Humorous. Hence «лезилебовић» - a lazybones. Often «леб» without «х»: common in everyday speech and writing.

forms: literally: good as a little loaf

examples.sr: Њен деда је [до̏бар ка̏о ле́бац].
examples.en: Her grandfather is as good as gold.

examples.sr: Радио је за [на̀сушни хле̏б].
examples.en: He worked for his daily bread.

note: From the Lord's Prayer: «хлеб наш насушни дај нам данас».

meanings: to welcome with bread and salt

examples.sr: Код нас се гости [дочѐкују хле̏бом и со̀љу].
examples.en: Here, guests are welcomed with bread and salt.

meanings: to want more than one needs
forms: literally: to ask for bread on top of flatbread

examples.sr: Има посао и кућу, а још [тра̏жи хле̏ба пре̏ко пога̀че].
examples.en: He has a job and a house, and he still wants more.

note: Погача is a flatbread; bread on top of it is too much. «То је хлеб преко погаче» - that is excess.

forms: literally: to go after the hand

examples.sr: Коначно ми је [по̏шло за ру́ко̄м] да положим испит.
examples.en: I finally managed to pass the exam.

note: Impersonal: person (dat.) + је пошло за руком.

forms: literally: to enter into the years

examples.sr: Мој деда је [за̀шао у го̏дине], али је и даље бодар.
examples.en: My grandfather is getting on in years, but he's still sprightly.

examples.sr: Нисам могао да [вѐрујем сво̀јӣм у̀шима] кад сам чуо вест.
examples.en: I couldn't believe my ears when I heard the news.

meanings: to hear with one's own ears

examples.sr: То сам [чу̏о сво̀јӣм у̀шима], нико ми није препричао.
examples.en: I heard that with my own ears, nobody told it to me.

meanings: to listen with half an ear

examples.sr: Он ме [слу̏ша на је̏дно у̏во] док гледа телефон.
examples.en: He listens to me with half an ear while looking at his phone.

note: Variant: «слушати са пола ува».

examples.sr: Не причај о томе овде, [и зи̏дови и̏мају у̏ши].
examples.en: Don't talk about it here, walls have ears.

meanings: to blush up to one's ears

examples.sr: Девојчица је [по̀црвенела до у̀шијӯ] кад су је похвалили.
examples.en: The little girl blushed up to her ears when they praised her.

forms: literally: to rip ears

examples.sr: Њен нагласак ми [па̀ра у̏ши].
examples.en: Her accent grates on my ears.

key: phr:један плус три једнако је четири

examples.sr: [Пе̑т ми́нус два̑ је̏дна̄ко је три̑].
examples.en: Five minus two equals three.

examples.sr: [Пе̑т пу̏та два̑ је̏дна̄ко је де̏сет].
examples.en: Five times two equals ten.

note: Плус, минус, пута (times), подељено са (divided by). The result comes after «једнако је».

forms: literally: to swear like a coachman

examples.sr: Кад је видео штету, [псо̀вао] је као кочијаш.
examples.en: When he saw the damage, he swore like a trooper.

key: phr:ко о чему, баба о уштипцима
forms: literally: each about something, the old woman about fritters

examples.sr: Опет прича о храни - [ко̏ о чѐму, ба̏ба о у̀штипцима].
examples.en: Talking about food again - some people only ever think of one thing.

note: About a person obsessed with one topic. Уштипци are fried pieces of dough.

key: phr:трла баба лан да јој прође дан
meanings: to fritter time away on trifles
forms: literally: the old woman beat flax to make the day pass

examples.sr: Цео дан смо седели и причали - [тр́ла ба̏ба ла̏н]!
examples.en: We sat and talked all day - just killing time!

note: About an activity with no result, only to kill time.

key: phr:што је баби мило, то јој се и снило
meanings: you see what you want to see
people dream of what is on their mind
forms: literally: what the old woman likes is what she dreams of

examples.sr: Он у свему види превару - [што̏ је ба̀би ми̏ло, то̑ јој се и сни̏ло].
examples.en: He sees deception in everything - you see what's on your mind.

note: Said with a touch of folk irony.

forms: literally: to play with fire

examples.sr: Немој да [се и̏гра̄ш ва̏тром]!
examples.en: Don't play with fire!

meanings: to pull someone's chestnuts out of the fire
forms: literally: to take chestnuts out of the fire

examples.sr: Увек ја морам да [ва̏дим ке̏стење из ва̏тре].
examples.en: I always have to pull the chestnuts out of the fire.

note: Often about a politician who sorts out a conflict he did not start.

meanings: to get on one's last nerve
forms: literally: to climb to the top of the head

examples.sr: Та песма ми се већ [по̀пела на вр̏х гла́ве].
examples.en: I'm already sick of that song.

note: Also without a verb: «Ово ми је на врх главе» - I've had enough.

forms: literally: a meeting at the top

examples.sr: Сутра почиње [са̀станак на вр̀ху] председника држава.
examples.en: A summit of the heads of state starts tomorrow.

forms: literally: it is peeing to me

examples.sr: [Пи̏шки ми се], станимо на следећој пумпи.
examples.en: I need to pee, let's stop at the next gas station.

note: Colloquial, children's or everyday speech; the construction is like «спава ми се».

forms: literally: to move on to the matter

examples.sr: Хајде да [прѐђемо на ства̑р].
examples.en: Let's get to the point.

note: Imperative: «Пређи на ствар!»

forms: literally: smeared with all the colors

examples.sr: Не верујем му, он је [прѐмазан сви̑м бо̀јама].
examples.en: I don't trust him, he's a sly old fox.

note: The image of a chameleon: a person who changes color to suit the situation.

meanings: to put in a rosy light
forms: literally: to show in a pink color

examples.sr: Он увек [прика̀зује ства̀ри у ру̀жичастој бо̀ји].
examples.en: He always paints a rosy picture of things.

note: The paired phrase is «приказати у црној боји».

forms: literally: to see in black colors

examples.sr: Ти све [ви̏дӣш у цр̀ним бо̀јама].
examples.en: You see everything in black.

note: Also «приказати у црној боји» - to portray in a gloomy light.

forms: literally: to burst into laughter

examples.sr: Кад је чула шалу, [пра̀сла је у сме̑х].
examples.en: When she heard the joke, she burst out laughing.

note: About sudden, unexpected laughter; can add «против воље» - against one's will.

forms: literally: to pour from the hollow into the empty

examples.sr: Цео састанак су [прѐсипали из шу̏пљег у пра̑зно].
examples.en: They spent the whole meeting spinning their wheels.

note: About people who look busy but achieve nothing.

meanings: to build castles in the air
forms: literally: to build towers in the air

examples.sr: Не [зи̑да̄ј ку̀ле у ва̀здуху], већ почни да радиш.
examples.en: Don't build castles in the air, get to work.

note: Suggests groundless dreams and plans with no basis.

forms: literally: to do the work of Sisyphus

examples.sr: Чистимо, а деца све растуре - [ра̀димо Си̏зифов по̀сао].
examples.en: We clean and the kids scatter everything again - it's a Sisyphean task.

note: From the Greek myth; often «То је Сизифов посао».

meanings: to have everything handed to one on a plate
forms: literally: to come to the ready-made

examples.sr: Он очекује да ће [до́ћи на го̀тово].
examples.en: He expects to have everything handed to him on a plate.

forms: literally: a finished thing

examples.sr: Одлука је пала, то је већ [го̀това ства̑р].
examples.en: The decision has been made, it's already a done deal.

note: «Готов» here means finished.

meanings: can I try it on? (in a shop)
forms: literally: may I try

examples.sr: Свиђа ми се ова јакна. [Мо̀гу ли да је про̑бам]?
examples.en: I like this jacket. Can I try it on?

note: A must-have phrase in a clothes shop; a fitting room is «кабина за пробу».

forms: literally: with working days

examples.sr: [Ра̑дним да́нима] устајем у шест.
examples.en: On weekdays I get up at six.

note: «викендом» (on weekends) and «празницима» (on holidays) are built the same way, in the instrumental: a regular action.

forms: literally: a free workplace

examples.sr: У нашој фирми има [сло̏бодно ра̑дно ме̏сто].
examples.en: There is a job opening at our company.

note: For remote work people say «рад од куће» or «посао од куће».

forms: literally: don't count it as a fault

examples.sr: [Не замѐри], био сам нервозан.
examples.en: Don't hold it against me, I was nervous.

note: Polite form: «не замерите». Smooths over a small awkwardness.

forms: literally: my mistake

examples.sr: [Мо̀ја гре̏шка], нисам правилно разумео.
examples.en: My mistake, I didn't understand correctly.

note: Fuller: «грешка је моја». Admits responsibility.

meanings: I didn't mean to offend you
forms: literally: I didn't want to offend you

examples.sr: [Ни́сам хтѐла да те у̀вредим], извини.
examples.en: I didn't mean to offend you, sorry.

note: A woman says «нисам хтела». Stresses that the words were not meant badly.

forms: literally: to wait one's fill

examples.sr: [На̀чекали смо се] у реду.
examples.en: We waited and waited in line.

note: The prefix «на-» and «се» show that the wait dragged on and was tiring.

forms: literally: to spare time

examples.sr: Онлајн куповина [штѐди вре́ме].
examples.en: Shopping online saves time.

note: Also «штедети новац, енергију» (save money, energy).

forms: literally: to wait in line

examples.sr: Не волим да [че̏кам у ре̏ду].
examples.en: I don't like waiting in line.

key: phr:питати за савет у вези са
forms: literally: to ask for advice in connection with

examples.sr: Желим да [пи̑та̄м за са́вет у ве́зи са] возовима.
examples.en: I want to ask for advice about trains.

note: «у вези са» + instr. means 'regarding, in connection with'.

forms: literally: the year's times

examples.sr: Која су ти омиљена [го̀дишња до̑ба]?
examples.en: Which are your favorite seasons?

note: «доба» is neuter (pl. «доба»). The seasons: пролеће, лето, јесен, зима.

forms: literally: at no price whatever

examples.sr: Тамо не бих ишао [ни по ко̀јӯ цѐну].
examples.en: I wouldn't go there for anything.

note: An emphatic refusal. More jokingly: «ни под тачком разно» (under no circumstances).

forms: literally: not under the item «miscellaneous»

examples.sr: Позајмити му новац? [Ни под та̏чком ра̏зно]!
examples.en: Lend him money? Not on your life!

note: From meeting agendas, where «разно» is the last item (any other business). Sounds more ironic than «никако».

forms: literally: a non-working day

examples.sr: Сутра је [не̏радни да̑н], продавнице не раде.
examples.en: Tomorrow is a day off, the shops are closed.

note: A notice on a door. One's own day off is «слободан дан»; a holiday is «празник».

forms: literally: on prescription

examples.sr: Овај лек се издаје само [на рѐцепт].
examples.en: This medicine is dispensed only on prescription.

note: Without a prescription: «без рецепта».

forms: literally: poured beer

examples.sr: Овде имају добро [то̀чено пи̑во].
examples.en: They have good draft beer here.

note: From «точити» - to pour. Dark beer is «тамно», light is «светло».

meanings: he who sings means no harm
forms: literally: whoever sings thinks no evil

examples.sr: Увек пева, па [ко̏ пе̏ва, зло̏ не ми̏сли].
examples.en: He's always singing, and he who sings means no harm.

meanings: history is the teacher of life

examples.sr: [Ѝсто̄рија је учитѐљица живо̀та], али ђаци су лоши.
examples.en: History is the teacher of life, but the pupils are bad.

meanings: Where can I park my car?

examples.sr: Извините, [где̏ мо̀гу да па̀ркирам а̀уто]?
examples.en: Excuse me, where can I park my car?

note: A possible answer: «Недалеко одавде имате паркинг» - there is a parking lot not far from here.

examples.sr: Одлично радите, [наста̀вите та̀ко̄]!
examples.en: You're doing great work, keep it up!

meanings: I'd like to open an account.

examples.sr: Добар дан, [жѐлео бих да о̀творим ра̀чӯн].
examples.en: Good afternoon, I'd like to open an account.

note: A woman says «желела бих».

examples.sr: Где је мењачница? [Тре́ба да про̀меним но̀вац].
examples.en: Where is the exchange office? I need to exchange money.

examples.sr: Молим вас, [да̑јте ми си̏тне но̀вчанице].
examples.en: Please give me small bills.

examples.sr: [Потпѝшите на по̀леђини], молим вас.
examples.en: Please sign on the back.

forms: literally: the train ran away from me

examples.sr: [По̀бегао ми је во̑з], па чекам следећи.
examples.en: I missed my train, so I'm waiting for the next one.

key: phr:да ли је ово седиште заузето

examples.sr: Извините, [да ли је о̀во̄ се̏дӣште за̀узето]?
examples.en: Excuse me, is this seat taken?

key: phr:на којој станици треба да сиђем
meanings: Which stop should I get off at?

examples.sr: [На ко̀јо̄ј ста̀ници тре́ба да сѝђем] за музеј?
examples.en: Which stop should I get off at for the museum?

examples.sr: [На у̀глу скрѐните ле̑во], па право.
examples.en: Turn left at the corner, then go straight.

examples.sr: Не журиш? [Пожу̀ри пола́ко], има времена.
examples.en: Not in a hurry? Make haste slowly, there's plenty of time.

note: A proverb: rushing does not help the job.

key: phr:добар глас далеко иде, а зао још даље
meanings: A good name travels far, a bad one even farther.

examples.sr: Пази шта причаш, [до̏бар гла̑с далѐко и̏де, а за̏о јо̏ш да̏ље̄].
examples.en: Watch what you say: a good name travels far, and a bad one even farther.

forms: literally: turn on all four

examples.sr: Станите на ивицу и [у̀кључите сва̏ чѐтири].
examples.en: Pull over to the side and turn on your hazard lights.

note: Colloquial name for the hazard lights: all four turn signals.

forms: literally: I don't even have a broken para

examples.sr: [Не̑ма̄м ни прѐбијене па̀ре] до плате.
examples.en: I don't have a penny until payday.

examples.sr: [Ка̀ква је прогно́за за су̏тра]? Хоће ли бити киша?
examples.en: What's the forecast for tomorrow? Will it rain?

examples.sr: [На̏пољу па̏да ки̏ша], узми кишобран.
examples.en: It's raining outside, take an umbrella.

note: Likewise: «пада снег» (it's snowing).

examples.sr: [Вру̑ће је да̀нас, за̏р не]?
examples.en: It's hot today, isn't it?

note: «зар не» is a colloquial «isn't it».

examples.sr: [Ба̏вим се спо̏ртом] три пута недељно.
examples.en: I play sports three times a week.

note: «бавити се» takes the instrumental: бавити се музиком, фотографијом.

key: phr:он је мирођија у свакој чорби
meanings: He pokes his nose into everything.
forms: literally: he is the dill in every soup

examples.sr: Он увек коментарише, [миро̀ђија у сва̀кој чо́рбӣ].
examples.en: He always has a comment, he pokes his nose into everything.

note: About a person who meddles in everything.

key: phr:нека ти нова година донесе све о чему машташ
meanings: May the New Year bring you everything you dream of.

examples.sr: [Не̏ка ти Но̑ва го̏дина до̀несе све̏ о чѐму ма̏шташ]!
examples.en: May the New Year bring you everything you dream of!

note: It usually goes on: «и нека ти се оствари све што пожелиш» - and may everything you wish come true.

examples.sr: Размисли пре одлуке: [се̏дам пу̏та ме̏ри, јѐдно̄м се́ци].
examples.en: Think before you decide: measure twice, cut once.

key: phr:у свакој шали има пола истине
meanings: There is some truth in every joke.

examples.sr: Смејали су се, али [у сва̀кој ша̀ли и̏ма по́ла и̏стине].
examples.en: They laughed, but there is some truth in every joke.

meanings: When choosing a wife, look at her mother.

examples.sr: Деда каже: [гле̏да̄ј ма̏јку, бѝрај ћѐрку].
examples.en: Grandpa says: look at the mother, choose the daughter.

note: Advice to a groom: the mother shows what the future wife will be like.

key: phr:она је метар и шумска јагода
forms: literally: she is a meter and a wild strawberry

examples.sr: Мала је, [о̀на је ме̏тар и шу̏мска ја̏года].
examples.en: She's tiny, pint-sized.

note: A joking way to speak of a short woman.

examples.sr: [По̀здрави] маму од мене!
examples.en: Say hi to Mom for me!

note: «поздравити» + acc.

meanings: the sky and the earth merged (awful weather)

examples.sr: Док смо возили, [са̀ставило се не̏бо са зѐмљо̄м].
examples.en: While we were driving, the heavens opened.

examples.sr: Ту [за̀брањено је парки́ра̄ње].
examples.en: Parking is prohibited here.

note: Signs often leave out «је»: «Забрањено паркирање».

meanings: no matter what I do (it won't work)
forms: literally: drop dead, burst

examples.sr: Хоћу визу, али [цр̀кни, пу̏кни], не иде.
examples.en: I want a visa, but no matter what I do, it won't work.

note: Not a swear word: it expresses frustration when something won't work out.

examples.sr: Које је расе? [Мо̀гу ли да га по̀мазим]?
examples.en: What breed is he? Can I pet him?

examples.sr: Извините, [да ли ва̏ш па̑с у̀једа]?
examples.en: Excuse me, does your dog bite?

examples.sr: - Преселио се у другу земљу. - [Мо̏лӣм]?!
examples.en: - He moved to another country. - What?!

note: Also 'please', 'hello?' (answering the phone) and 'you're welcome' in reply to «хвала».

forms: literally: I keep running

examples.sr: Да ти донесем кафу? - [Све̏ тр̏чим]!
examples.en: Shall I bring you a coffee? - Yeah, right, I'm on my way!

note: A sarcastic refusal.

examples.sr: [Ѝма̄м по̏здра̄в од Мѝлице].
examples.en: Milica says hi.

meanings: How do you say it in Serbian?

examples.sr: [Ка̀ко се ка̏же на ср̏пском] «спасибо»?
examples.en: How do you say «thank you» in Serbian?

examples.sr: Извините, ја сам странац, [го̀ворите пола́ко].
examples.en: Excuse me, I'm a foreigner, please speak slowly.

examples.sr: [Шта̏ зна̑чи о̀ва̄ ре̑ч]?
examples.en: What does this word mean?

examples.sr: Не осећам мирис, [но̑с ми је за̀пушен].
examples.en: I can't smell anything, my nose is blocked.

examples.sr: Не идем на посао, [ѝма̄м висо̀ку температу́ру].
examples.en: I'm not going to work, I have a high fever.

examples.sr: Јутрос [бо̀ли ме гр̏ло].
examples.en: My throat hurts this morning.

note: «боли ме» + subject: боли ме глава, боле ме леђа (pl.).

forms: literally: my suitcase is full

examples.sr: Стално исто, [пу̏н ми је ку̀фер]!
examples.en: Always the same thing, I'm fed up!

meanings: I've had it up to here!
forms: literally: my hat is full

examples.sr: [Пу̀на ми је ка̏па] те гужве!
examples.en: I've had it up to here with this crowd!

note: A variant of «Пун ми је куфер»; «капа» is feminine.

forms: literally: your hot sun

examples.sr: [Су̑нце ти жа́рко], опет сам закаснио!
examples.en: Darn it, I'm late again!

note: A mild substitute for a rude swear word.

examples.sr: [И̏маш лѐпе о̏чи] и леп осмех.
examples.en: You have beautiful eyes and a lovely smile.

examples.sr: [Ди̏вно и̏згледаш] у том оделу.
examples.en: You look wonderful in that suit.

meanings: You have a good sense of humor.

examples.sr: [И̏маш до̏бар сми̑сао за ху̀мор], волим да се смејем.
examples.en: You have a good sense of humor, I love to laugh.

examples.sr: Хвала на поруци, [у̀лепшала си ми да̑н]!
examples.en: Thanks for the message, you made my day!

note: To a woman: «улепшала си ми дан».

examples.sr: Комшија, [до̀ђите на ка̀фу] у недељу!
examples.en: Neighbor, come over for coffee on Sunday!

note: A common invitation to neighbors.

key: phr:драго ми је што смо комшије

examples.sr: [Дра̑го ми је што̏ смо ко̀мшије], зови ако треба помоћ.
examples.en: I'm glad we're neighbors, call if you need help.

examples.sr: Извините, [мо̀гу ли да вам по̀могнем]?
examples.en: Excuse me, can I help you?

meanings: Give me half a kilo of apples.

examples.sr: Молим вас, [да̑јте ми по́ла ки̏лограма ја̏бука].
examples.en: Please give me half a kilo of apples.

note: After a quantity, the genitive: пола килограма јабука.

examples.sr: Хвала, [пла̏ћам ка̀ртицом].
examples.en: Thanks, I'll pay by card.

examples.sr: Извините, [да ли и̏мате си̏тно]?
examples.en: Excuse me, do you have change?

examples.sr: [Ко̀јӣ је ро̏к тра̀јања] овог сира?
examples.en: What's the shelf life of this cheese?

key: phr:да ли овај аутобус иде на аеродром
meanings: Does this bus go to the airport?

examples.sr: [Да ли о̀ва̄ј ауто́бус и̏де на аеро̀дром]?
examples.en: Does this bus go to the airport?

meanings: Where do I need to change?

examples.sr: [Где̏ тре́ба да прѐседнем] за центар?
examples.en: Where do I change to get to the center?

examples.sr: Помогао си ми око селидбе, [ба̏ш си ца̏р]!
examples.en: You helped me with the move, you're the man!

note: To a woman: «Баш си царица!».

forms: literally: you're hammering like a Maxim gun at a division

examples.sr: Земља је равна? [Лу̀паш ко̏ Ма̏ксим по дивѝзији]!
examples.en: The Earth is flat? You're talking nonsense!

note: A joking reply to nonsense; «лупати» also means to talk rubbish. Maxim is a machine gun.

forms: literally: like a boiled leg

examples.sr: Тај кандидат ми је [ка̏о ку̏вана но̀га].
examples.en: That candidate leaves me cold.

note: About a person with no spark and no opinion.

key: phr:ко се чува, и бог га чува

examples.sr: Понеси кишобран, [ко̏ се чу̏ва, и Бо̑г га чу̏ва].
examples.en: Take an umbrella, better safe than sorry.

meanings: winter is nothing to fear when there is ajvar

examples.sr: Спремио сам теглице, [не̑ма зи́ме ка̑д и̏ма ајва́ра].
examples.en: I've prepared the jars, winter is nothing to fear when there is ajvar.

note: A humorous saying: pepper preserves make for a well-fed winter. Ајвар is a roasted red pepper spread.

examples.sr: Остани мирно, [не мр̏дај], снимамо зуб.
examples.en: Stay still, don't move, we're taking an X-ray of your tooth.

note: Often heard at the dentist.

examples.sr: [Ѝма̄м сре̏ће], одмах сам нашао паркинг.
examples.en: I'm lucky, I found parking right away.

note: «Немам среће» - I'm out of luck.

examples.sr: Не бој се, [сре̏ћа пра̏ти хра̏бре].
examples.en: Don't be afraid, fortune favors the brave.

key: phr:три ствари се не могу сакрити: љубав, сиромаштво и кашаљ
meanings: Three things cannot be hidden: love, poverty and a cough.

examples.sr: Како је рекао Андрић, [три̑ ства̀ри се не мо̀гу са̀крити: љу́бав, сирома́штво и ка̏шаљ].
examples.en: As Andrić said, three things cannot be hidden: love, poverty and a cough.

note: A thought of Ivo Andrić, the Nobel Prize-winning writer.

forms: literally: he grabbed his head

examples.sr: Када је видео рачун, [у̀хватио се за гла̑ву].
examples.en: When he saw the bill, he clutched his head.

note: More often shows great surprise or shock, not only despair.

key: phr:волим те до месеца и назад
meanings: I love you to the moon and back.

examples.sr: [Во̏лӣм те до ме̏сеца и на̏за̄д]!
examples.en: I love you to the moon and back!

key: phr:срце ми куца само за тебе
meanings: My heart beats only for you.

examples.sr: [Ср̏це ми ку́ца са̏мо за те̏бе].
examples.en: My heart beats only for you.

examples.sr: Напољу [вѐје сне̑г], остани код куће.
examples.en: There's a blizzard outside, stay home.

examples.sr: Обуци капут, [ле̏дено је]!
examples.en: Put on your coat, it's freezing!

meanings: I wish you all the best!

examples.sr: За рођендан, [жѐлим ти све̏ на̏јлепше]!
examples.en: Happy birthday, I wish you all the best!

key: phr:нека ти се све жеље остваре
meanings: May all your wishes come true!

examples.sr: [Не̏ка ти се све̏ же̏ље о̀стваре] у новој години!
examples.en: May all your wishes come true in the new year!

examples.sr: Торта је добра, [је̏лда]?
examples.en: The cake is good, right?

examples.sr: Данас је лепо време, [је̏лда]?
examples.en: The weather is nice today, isn't it?

note: Short for «је ли да». Goes at the end of a sentence. Also «јел' да».

forms: literally: the drop that made the cup overflow

examples.sr: Његово кашњење била је [ка̑п ко̀ја̄ је прѐлила ча̏шу].
examples.en: His lateness was the last straw.

examples.sr: Та увреда је била [ка̑п ко̀ја̄ је прѐлила ча̏шу].
examples.en: That insult was the last straw.

forms: literally: an idle priest even baptizes kids

examples.sr: Целог дана преуређује полице - [до̀кон по̏п и јарѝће кр̏сти].
examples.en: He spends all day rearranging the shelves - idle hands find work.

examples.sr: Није имао посла, па је опрао и гаражу: [до̀кон по̏п и јарѝће кр̏сти].
examples.en: He had nothing to do, so he even washed the garage: idle hands find work.

note: Proverb about idleness: a bored priest even baptizes kid goats (јарић - young goat).

forms: literally: you have no worry

examples.sr: Заборавио сам хлеб! - [Не̑маш бри̏ге], већ сам купила.
examples.en: I forgot the bread! - Don't worry, I already bought some.

examples.sr: [Не̑маш бри̏ге], ја ћу то средити.
examples.en: Don't worry, I'll sort it out.

note: A softer alternative: «не брини».
